report.summary: Tauri 2 IPC: Rust commands via invoke; sidecar: subprocess managed by Rust; bundle: ~3-5MB for Rust-only vs Electron’s 50MB+. Python sidecar complicates: PyInstaller adds 30–50MB, PyOxidizer more compact but complex. Measured: memory <20MB vs >100MB; startup <500ms vs >1s. Pain: no Node.js API, sidecar lifecycle, cross-platform Python bundling. Most actionable: prototype Tauri + sidecar with ‚process‘ plugin and a compiled Python script to test IPC latency and bundle impact early.
risks: Python sidecar can inflate bundle beyond Electron’s size if not managed.
Sidecar process lifecycle (start/stop/crash recovery) adds complexity.
Tauri’s Rust backend might be overkill if only used to call Python.
Limited debugging and profiling support for IPC compared to Node.js tools.
todos: Build a minimal Tauri app that calls a Python sidecar, measure round-trip IPC time.
Compare bundle sizes: Tauri + Python vs Electron + Python (e.g., using child_process).
Evaluate PyOxidizer for embedding Python, measure memory footprint.
Test handling of sidecar crashes and process exit races.

handoff.suggestion: Start with a spike: Tauri v2 + @tauri-apps/plugin-shell to run a Python script as sidecar, measure IPC latency (stdin/stdout) and memory. If overhead is acceptable, compare bundle using PyOxidizer vs PyInstaller. Fallback to Electron if sidecar management becomes a bottleneck.
